content: Cefixime, marketed as Suprax, is a cephalosporin-class antibacterial medication. Its use should be restricted to treating infections that are either confirmed or strongly suspected to be caused by bacteria susceptible to cefixime. This approach is essential to minimize the development of drug-resistant bacteria and to preserve the efficacy of cefixime and other antibacterial agents. When available, culture and susceptibility data should guide the selection or adjustment of antimicrobial therapy. In cases where such data are unavailable, local epidemiological trends and bacterial susceptibility patterns can inform empirical treatment decisions. Cefixime is approved for use in adults and pediatric patients aged six months or older for the treatment of the following infections caused by susceptible bacterial strains: 1. Uncomplicated Urinary Tract Infections (UTIs): Cefixime is effective against uncomplicated UTIs caused by Escherichia coli and Proteus mirabilis. 2. Otitis Media (Middle Ear Infections): Cefixime is indicated for otitis media caused by Haemophilus influenzae, Moraxella catarrhalis, and Streptococcus pyogenes. However, it is important to note that the efficacy of cefixime against Streptococcus pyogenes in this context has been studied in fewer than 10 cases. Additionally, for otitis media caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae, the overall response rate to cefixime was approximately 10% lower compared to the comparator drug. 3. Pharyngitis and Tonsillitis: Cefixime is effective in treating pharyngitis and tonsillitis caused by Streptococcus pyogenes. However, penicillin remains the standard treatment for infections caused by Streptococcus pyogenes. While cefixime is generally effective in eradicating Streptococcus pyogenes from the nasopharynx, there is no evidence to support its efficacy in preventing subsequent rheumatic fever. 4. Acute Exacerbations of Chronic Bronchitis: Cefixime is indicated for acute exacerbations of chronic bronchitis caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae. 5. Uncomplicated Gonorrhea (Cervical/Urethral): Cefixime is effective in treating uncomplicated gonorrhea (cervical or urethral infections) caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae, including both penicillinase-producing and non-penicillinase-producing strains.
